description: We're a team of university students passionate about space tech and software. For the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts" challenge, we're building a real-time dashboard that tracks astronauts' vital signs (heart rate, oxygen, sleep, stress) and alerts the crew to anomalies. Looking for: frontend/UI designers, developers, ML/data enthusiasts, and anyone interested in health tech. Beginners welcome, come build with us!
summary:
Nominal is a crew health monitoring prototype for long-duration space missions. Far from Earth, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for noticing health changes in themselves, and from a Mars base a message to flight surgeons and its reply take about 24 minutes, so the crew has to act first.

Nominal gives each astronaut a wrist display with their own readings, colour- and shape-coded by status, and clear guidance on what each value means and what to do. A tablet adds trends, lab results, nutrition, radiation dose and an alertness check. A shared cabin screen shows only the alerts that need crew action, and the crew medical officer gets a detailed view of everyone.

Four alert levels (nominal, caution, warning, critical) decide who is told: nominal and caution stay on the astronaut's own watch, a warning adds the medical officer, and a critical alert adds the whole crew and Earth.

The prototype uses NASA DONKI space weather data and NASA OSDR lab data; all physiological readings are simulated.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Nominal is a crew health monitoring prototype for long-duration space missions. Far from Earth, astronauts have to notice health changes in themselves. Nominal gives each crew member a wrist display with their own readings and clear guidance, a tablet with detailed trends, a shared cabin screen that shows only what needs the crew, and a detailed view for the crew medical officer.

HOW IT WORKS

- Watch: each astronaut sees only their own indicators, colour-coded by status, with an explanation of each value and what to do, plus a help button.

- Escalation: four alert levels (nominal, caution, warning, critical) decide who is told — nominal and caution stay on the astronaut's own watch, a warning adds the crew medical officer, and a critical alert adds the whole crew and flight surgeons on Earth, with realistic communication delay.

- Early warning: when a reading drifts steadily away from the crew member's own baseline, the watch shows how soon it will reach the next alert level, so the crew can act before the alert.

- Suit sensors and body map: during a spacewalk, sensors report helmet CO2, water in the helmet, fingertip temperature and suit contact pressure; a clickable body map shows the region that needs attention.

- Crew response: each alert carries a response checklist that anyone on board ticks off. In a spacewalk emergency the commander or medical officer can pull the crew member back to the airlock by the safety tether.

- Also included: a 30-second alertness check modelled on the psychomotor vigilance test, a personal radiation dose tracker, blood panel results, nutrition logging from the ISS standard menu, messages to Earth, and a live 3D simulation of the vehicle and crew.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

On a Mars mission a message to Earth and its reply take about 24 minutes, so the crew has to act first. Nominal is designed so that each astronaut can assess their own health, understands what a value means and what to do next, and so that the right people are told at the right time without exposing routine health values to the whole crew.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

React and TypeScript single-page app built with Vite; three.js with React Three Fiber for the 3D view; Firebase Realtime Database and anonymous authentication for live sync between devices; Vitest for tests; hosted on Cloudflare Pages. A deterministic simulator generates the indicator values from time, so every screen shows the same numbers.

NASA DATA

NASA DONKI space weather data (solar particle events raise a radiation advisory), NASA Open Science Data Repository study OSD-575 (Inspiration4 metabolic panel, used for glucose baselines and lab results), the ISS Standard Menu nutritional data, NASA Human Research Program hazard and risk material, and the NASA 3D Resources astronaut model. Canadian Space Agency resources on radiation monitoring and the Bio-Monitor smart shirt were also used.

CREATIVITY

One health event can be followed live across every device: a guided one-minute tour plays a spacewalker's blood oxygen drifting down and shows who is told at each step, from the astronaut's own watch to flight surgeons on Earth. The 3D mission view lets you move crew between modules, the airlock and a spacewalk and watch every screen follow.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

- Privacy: routine health values stay private; the cabin screen shows only critical alerts and help calls, and the commander sees duty status without health values.

- Accessibility: alert levels have a shape as well as a colour, so they do not depend on colour vision.

- Autonomy: the crew acts first because of signal delay; in a real vehicle the devices would share data over the vehicle's own network.

- Honesty about limits: all physiological data is simulated, and thresholds are prototype values that are not clinically validated.


REFERENCES


The full list of data sources, scientific papers, libraries, services and tools is in the project README: https://github.com/muratcanaykan/nominal#other-references

Live app: https://nominal.rteuceng.com
